function: Predictive joint design of the ISAC transmit waveform and receive filter of a satellite from historical channel data, maximizing weighted communications and sensing rates (p. 1).
system: Satellite ISAC with 3x3 UPA transmit and 3x3 UPA radar-receive arrays, K=3 ground IoT devices, Q=3 moving targets, full duplex, 11 GHz, no RIS (p. 9).
method: PONet: CNN layers plus Transformer encoder predicting waveform and filter from historical CSI and target-response matrices; unsupervised training on the weighted-rate loss (pp. 7-8).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician satellite channel with distance-based gain, random ground-device and moving-target positions in a 20x20 km area; 2,000 samples, 80/20 train/test split (pp. 3, 9).
test_conditions: Same system settings for training and testing on a 20% held-out split; sweeps of communications weight, history length tau, data samples and signal length L (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Learned: EPDNet, HCLNet, ISACNN (CNN/LSTM predictors, retrained); non-learned: random waveform and filter (p. 10).
metrics: Communications rate and sensing rate (bits/s/Hz), training and testing loss, transmit and filter power (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Online inference O(L_E tau eta_t^2), offline O(I_max N_s L_E tau eta_t^2), Transformer-dominated; no measured runtime or parameter count (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 3: "we model satellite channel model with Rician fading" - a custom simulator following refs [18], [34], [37]; no 3GPP TR 38.811 model and no measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "divided into training and testing datasets" - the data are simulated from one setting and split 80/20; no scenario, band, array size or site outside the training setting is tested, and the sweeps (pp. 10-11) do not state testing a trained model under other conditions.
q3_support: p. 10: "Random: This method generates random transmit" waveforms and filters (non-learned) and p. 10: "EPDNet [25]: This approach employs a CNN to capture" (earlier learned method); p. 11: "PONet consistently achieves the highest communications and sensing rates".
q4_support: p. 9: "the Transformer encoder dominates" - Section IV-D gives the orders O(L_E tau eta_t^2) online and O(I_max N_s L_E tau eta_t^2) offline.
q5_support: p. 9: "The data is generated based on the system model" - simulated data; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 6: the learned transmit waveform (precoded over the 3x3 array) and receive filter control a satellite link that also senses, and the order of areas puts NTN (6) before ISAC (5). q1=0: custom Rician model with free-space gain (p. 3); the Rician factor value is not given. q3=1: the random waveform counts as the simple non-learned baseline; EPDNet, HCLNet and ISACNN are earlier learned designs adapted and retrained to this problem (footnote 12, p. 10). Table I (p. 9) is an image; its values (11 GHz, K=3, Q=3, L=10, tau=3) were read from the page image.
